scenes.title: Bottle email
scenes.caption: What it sends, and what switching it on takes.
scenes.say: Here's the email side of Message in a Bottle: what it can send, what works without it, and what turning it on costs.

scenes.title: Four emails
scenes.caption: Bottle can send four kinds of email.
scenes.say: Bottle can send four emails: an invitation, a sign in link, news of her notes, and word to you of new ones.

scenes.title: No email yet
scenes.caption: With no email set up, nothing leaves.
scenes.say: Right now no email account is set up, so every email sits in an outbox. You send Laura her link on WhatsApp instead.

scenes.title: Your side
scenes.caption: Your side needs no email at all.
scenes.say: Laura's notes land in the queue. Each one is done, held for you, or declined with a plain reason.

scenes.title: Email on
scenes.caption: Laura hears back by email too.
scenes.say: With email on, Laura gets one email listing her finished notes. It waits ten minutes, and never comes more than hourly.

scenes.title: Already safe
scenes.caption: The safety is already built in.
scenes.say: Link secrets stay hidden, scanners cannot use them up, and invitations last seven days. Turning someone off ends their links.

scenes.title: Cost
scenes.caption: About ten minutes, and nothing to pay.
scenes.say: Switching on takes about ten minutes with a personal Resend account. The free plan covers Laura's few emails, so it costs nothing.

scenes.title: My pick
scenes.caption: Start with no email. Switch on later.
scenes.say: My pick: start with no email. Send Laura her link on WhatsApp, and turn email on whenever you want her to hear back.

faults: scene 3: the phone is up in the air on the wall and no letter is seen going from You to Laura; a tick on Laura means nothing. Show the link sent by phone to her.
scene 4: a shield stands for 'three gates' and a tick for done, held, declined; the picture does not show notes being sorted.
scene 5: the server is labelled Bottle and its bar looks like a waiting meter but the letter never visibly reaches Laura; Laura is not clearly shown receiving one email.
scene 6: a letter stands for a link secret, a padlock is shown with a lock badge twice, and a calendar is labelled Laura in the ids; nothing shows scanners blocked or someone turned off.
scene 7: the clock icon has a clock badge on it (doubled), and the £0 is on the laptop but no time passes; the clock is too crowded.
scene 8: a cross on email and a tick on WhatsApp is fine, but the picture says email first is wrong when Peter says start without email then turn on later.
